findings.title: Other imports from "bun:bundle" are silently dropped and fail at runtime.
findings.body: The whole import statement becomes `S.Empty`, and only the `feature` specifier gets a declared symbol. `import * as b from "bun:bundle"` and default imports get no diagnostic at all. Other named specifiers only get a warning that says the value "will be undefined". In both cases the local name is never declared, so using it throws a `ReferenceError` at runtime (or resolves to an unrelated global) rather than being `undefined`. A second `feature` alias, which is reported as an error, is also left undeclared. Fix: report namespace, default and unknown specifiers as errors, or declare those bindings and assign them `undefined`.

findings.title: `BundleOptions.deinit` can free a StringSet it did not allocate.
findings.body: `transpiler.options.bundler_feature_flags` now points at `config.features`, which is a field inside the JSBundler config, not a separate heap allocation. The new `BundleOptions.deinit` frees any pointer that isn't the static empty set: it calls `deinit()` on it and then `allocator.destroy()`. If this transpiler is ever deinitialized, that is an invalid free of an embedded field. `config.deinit` then calls `features.deinit()` a second time. I could not see whether this transpiler's `deinit` actually runs. Fix: clone the set into its own allocation, or record whether the options own the set and only free it in that case.

findings.title: The runtime transpiler cache key ignores which feature flags are enabled.
findings.body: `bundler_feature_flags` now changes the transpiled output: `feature("X")` becomes `true` or `false`. It is not added to `hash_fields_for_runtime_transpiler`, and nothing else in the diff puts the flag set into the cache key. Trigger: run `bun run index.ts` on a file large enough to be cached, then run `bun run --feature=X index.ts`. The second run can reuse the cached output from the first and print the disabled branch. Fix: hash the sorted flag names into the cache key, or skip the runtime transpiler cache when any flags are set.

findings.title: The feature-flag set is built twice and the first copy leaks.
findings.body: `BundleOptions.fromApi` already builds the set from `transform.feature_flags`, which is `ctx.args.feature_flags` here. This line builds a second set and overwrites the pointer, so the first set is never freed. Drop this line, since `fromApi` already sets the field.
